'''Mandar Dnyaneshwar Agashe'''{{efn|{{IAST3|Maṃdāra Jñāneśvara Āgāśe}}. Agashe bears his father's name (Dnyaneshwar) as a middle name as per the [[patronymic]] [[Indian name#Marathi|Marathi naming conventions]],{{sfn|Agashe|Agashe|2006|page=62|loc=आगाशे, मंदार ज्ञानेश्वर}} but he is widely known without his patronymic.<ref name="SME Channels 1" /><ref name="Your Tech Story 1" />}} (born 24 May 1969) is an Indian businessman, music director, and former musician. He founded [[Sarvatra Technologies]] in 2000, and has served as the company's [[managing director]] since its inception.

As a musician, he is remembered for his [[Popular music|pop]] and [[rock music]] releases in [[Hindi]] and [[English language|English]] under [[Sony BMG]] in the 1990s and 2000s, and for [[music directing]] [[Marathi language|Marathi]] [[ghazal]] albums for [[Asha Bhosle]] in 2016, and [[Rahul Deshpande]] in 2021.

== Biography ==
=== Early life and family: 1969–1991 ===
Agashe was born on 24 May 1969 in [[Mumbai]], [[Maharashtra]],{{sfnm|1a1=Agashe|1a2=Agashe|1y=2006|1p=62|1loc=आगाशे, मंदार ज्ञानेश्वर|2a1=Ranade|2y=1974|2p=61}} into an aristocratic and entrepreneurial [[Chitpavan]] [[brahmin]] family of industrialist [[Dnyaneshwar Agashe]] of the [[Agashe]] ''[[Noble house (term)|gharana]]'' of [[Mangdari]],{{sfn|Ranade|1974|pages=59–60, 70}} and wife Rekha Gogte, of the Gogte ''gharana'' of [[Belgaum]].{{sfn|Kamath|1991|page=10}}

Through his father, Agashe is a grandson of [[Chandrashekhar Agashe]], a nephew of [[Panditrao Agashe]] and [[Shakuntala Karandikar]], an older brother of [[Ashutosh Agashe|Ashutosh]] and [[Sheetal Agashe]],{{sfn|Karandikar|1992|page=Illustration 20}} of distant relation to [[Third Anglo-Maratha War]] [[Army general|general]] [[Bapu Gokhale]],{{sfn|Pathak|1978|page=976}} musician [[Ashutosh Phatak]],{{sfn|Ranade|1982|page=56}} historian [[Dinkar G. Kelkar]], and scientist [[P. K. Kelkar]].{{Sfn|Kelkar|Kelkar|Kelkar|1993|pages=82, 89}} 

Through his mother, Agashe is a great-nephew of [[Raosaheb Gogte|B. M. Gogte]],{{sfn|Kamath|1991|page=10}} a first cousin to poet [[Rashmi Parekh]], a descendant of the aristocratic [[Latey family|Latey (Bhagwat) family]], and of relation to [[Kokuyo Camlin]] head [[Dilip Dandekar]], and academic [[Jyoti Gogte]].{{Sfnm|1a1=Gogaṭe Kulamaṇḍala|1y=2006|1p=532|2a1=Barve|2y=1982|2pp=170, 173}}

Agashe graduated with a [[Bachelor of Engineering|BE]] degree in [[software engineering]] from the [[Pune Institute of Computer Technology]] in 1990.<ref>{{cite web |title=Mandar Agashe alumni of 1990 batch, an entrepreneur, Music director and Singer |url=https://alumni.pict.edu/f/mandar-agashe-alumni-of-1990-batch-an-entrepreneur-music-director-and-singer-3788 |website=[[Pune Institute of Computer Technology]] |access-date=5 January 2022 |date=January 14, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220102145604/https://alumni.pict.edu/f/mandar-agashe-alumni-of-1990-batch-an-entrepreneur-music-director-and-singer-3788 |archive-date=2 January 2022}}</ref> He has been married to Aparna Pandharkar since 1996; she [[Maiden and married names#Name changes upon marriage|adopted the name]] Jiza Agashe upon marriage. They have two children.{{sfn|Agashe|Agashe|2006|page=62}}

=== Early business career: 1991–2008 ===
In 1991, Agashe was appointed to the [[board of directors]] at his grandfather's [[Brihan Maharashtra Sugar Syndicate]],<ref>{{Cite report |title=Director's Report of the Brihan Maharashtra Sugar Syndicate |date=3 October 1992 |last=Agashe |first=D. C. |author-link=Dnyaneshwar Agashe |location=[[Pune]] |page=1}}</ref> going on to become the [[managing director|joint managing director]] of the syndicate in 1994, the same year he was appointed a [[Director (business)|director]] on his father's [[Suvarna Sahakari Bank]].{{Sfn|Ministry of Commerce & Industry|1999|page=14}}<ref>{{Cite report |title=Director's Report of the Brihan Maharashtra Sugar Syndicate |date=9 August 1995 |last=Agashe |first=D. C. |author-link=Dnyaneshwar Agashe |location=[[Pune]] |page=2}}</ref> He founded a number of companies under the Brihans Group – Brihans Pharmaceuticals, an [[Ayurveda|ayurvedic medicine]] company in 1998,{{sfn|Ministry of Commerce & Industry|2000|page=13}} and ''musicurry.com'', an [[internet radio]] company in 1999,{{Sfn|Business World|2000|pages=24, 55–56}} the same year, he resigned as joint managing director of the syndicate.<ref>{{Cite report |title=Director's Report of the Brihan Maharashtra Sugar Syndicate |date=2 August 1999 |last=Limaye |first=Y. D. |location=[[Pune]] |page=3}}</ref>

By December 1999, Agashe and his [[CEO]] Gautam Godse had partnered with [[California]]-based software company Questionable Ventures to develop ''musicurry.com'',<ref>{{cite news |title=Curried music |work=The Sunday Review |agency=[[Times News Network|TNN]] |date=12 December 1999}}</ref> and in January 2000 he invited [[Usha Mangeshkar]] to be the internet radio's creative consultant,<ref>{{cite news |title=Musicurry.com comes as music to the ears |work=[[The Indian Express]] |agency=[[Indian Express Limited|ENS]] |date=14 January 2000}}</ref> with Agashe announcing plans to upload the [[Mangeshkar family]] archives to the web service by February–March 2000.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Seshan |first1=Sekhar |title=A question of music |journal=[[Business India]] |date=21 February 2000 |page=116 |issn=0254-5268 |oclc=4525594 |lccn=78914172}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Karnani |first1=Roop |title=The Melody of Money |journal=[[Business Today (India)|Business Today]] |date=22 February 2000 |pages=76–77 |lccn=92901481 |oclc=321079911}}</ref> The web service was officially launched on 13 January 2000.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Karim |first1=Ahmed |title=Making music? Hurry to MusicCurry! |work=[[The Times of India]] |date=13 February 2000}}</ref>

In April 2000, he founded [[Brihans Natural Products]], a [[skincare products]] manufacturing company,<ref name="Business India 1">{{cite journal |last=Seshan |first=Sekhar |title=A New High |journal=[[Business India]] |date=5-18 January 2004 |pages=69–70 |issue=674–679 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=qbBIAAAAYAAJ |access-date=16 February 2024 |publisher=A. H. Advani |issn=0254-5268 |oclc=4525594 |lccn=78914172 |via=[[University of Virginia]]}}</ref> and under him launched its signature [[aloe vera]] product range in 2002.<ref name="Business India 1" /> In June 2000, he established [[Sarvatra Technologies]], a company that developed [[banking software]] for Suvarna Sahakari Bank;<ref name="SME Channels 1">{{cite news |title=Mandar Agashe, Founder, MD and Vice Chairman, Sarvatra Technologies |url=https://www.smechannels.com/mandar-agashe-founder-md-and-vice-chairman-sarvatra-technologies/ |work=SMEChannels |date=2 February 2021 |access-date=9 October 2022 |oclc=980373179 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210221035025/https://www.smechannels.com/mandar-agashe-founder-md-and-vice-chairman-sarvatra-technologies/ |archive-date=21 February 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=New software boon for co-op. bank clients |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/pune/New-software-boon-for-co-op-bank-clients/articleshow/94360.cms |work=[[The Times of India]] |date=25 July 2003 |language=en |access-date=9 October 2022 |agency=[[Times News Network|TNN]] |location=[[Pune]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210804171643/https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/pune/New-software-boon-for-co-op-bank-clients/articleshow/94360.cms |archive-date=4 August 2021}}</ref> alongside his other [[financial technology]] companies, EBZ Online and Codito Technologies, also being founded in 2000.<ref name="Business India 1" />{{Sfn|Pan|2006|page=9}} In 2002, Agashe purchased stake in [[Deepak Ghaisas]]' [[I-flex Solutions]], after the company agreed to partner with Codito, with Ghaisas joining the board of directors.<ref>{{cite news |title=i-flex Solutions targets co-op banks |url=https://www.domain-b.com/finance/banks/200201jan/20020111_i-flex.html |access-date=27 April 2025 |work=[[The Hindu]] |date=11 January 2002 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20020204160236/http://domain-b.com/finance/banks/200201jan/20020111_i-flex.html |archive-date=4 February 2002}}</ref> In April 2002, he contributed an essay titled ''My Father'' to his father's [[festschrift]].{{sfn|Barve|Vartak|Belvalkar|2002|page=3|loc=''My Father'' – Mandar Agashe}}

In 2006, Agashe launched "Anywhere Money" [[POS terminal]]s under his company Saravatra Technologies to praise and support from politicians such as [[Shankarrao Gadakh]] in the [[Government of Maharashtra]].<ref name="Pudhari 1">{{cite news |title='एनी व्हेअर मनी' योजना देशभर राबविण्याची शिफारस : गडाख |work=[[Pudhari]] |date=18 August 2008 |location=[[Nagar taluka|Nagar]] |language=mr |trans-title=Recommendation to implement 'Anywhere Money' scheme across the country: Gadakh}}</ref> By 2007, Agashe had merged the business operations of EBZ Technologies and Codito with Sarvatra Technologies and partnered with [[Larry Ellison]] at the [[Oracle Corporation]] to introduce [[banking software]] technology to rural India,<ref>{{cite news |last1=Madhavan |first1=Narayanan |title=Larry, Mandar jam for rural banking |work=[[The Hindustan Times]] |date=11 May 2007 |location=[[New Delhi]] |via=[[Nicolaus Copernicus University in Toruń]]}}</ref> after the [[Reserve Bank of India]]'s governor [[Y. V. Reddy]] and economist [[Raghuram Rajan]] approved the plans in January 2008.<ref name="Pudhari 1" />

=== Suvarna Sahakari Bank scam allegations: 2008–2009 ===
{{main|Suvarna Sahakari Bank}}
In November 2008, Agashe was one of the directors implicated during [[Suvarna Sahakari Bank]]'s ₹4.3 billion [[Suvarna Sahakari Bank#2008 scam allegations|alleged scam case]].<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/pune/Agashe-others-sent-to-judicial-custody/articleshow/3753033.cms |title=Agashe, others sent to judicial custody |work=[[The Times of India]] |date=25 November 2008 |location=[[Pune]] |agency=[[Times News Network|TNN]] |access-date=9 October 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171127034029/https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/pune/Agashe-others-sent-to-judicial-custody/articleshow/3753033.cms |archive-date=27 November 2017}}</ref> His family, along with other [[Board of directors|board members]] of the bank, were arrested on the charges of alleged misuse of their rights to sanction [[loan]]s to firms owned by themselves and then [[Default (finance)|defaulting]] those loans, thereby [[Fraud|duping]] the bank's depositors.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.business-standard.com/article/finance/pune-coop-bank-in-rs-436-cr-scam-108112301024_1.html |title=Pune coop bank in Rs 436-cr scam |work=[[Business Standard]] |date=23 November 2008 |location=[[Pune]] |access-date=17 August 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160822112842/http://www.business-standard.com/article/finance/pune-coop-bank-in-rs-436-cr-scam-108112301024_1.html |archive-date=22 August 2016}}</ref> Agashe was in [[Germany]] at the time of the arrests, returning to India for his father's funeral in January 2009.<ref>{{cite news |title=Fugitive run ends for economic fraud and dreaded gangster |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/cities/pune/fugitive-run-ends-for-economic-fraud-and-dreaded-gangster/ |work=[[The Indian Express]] |agency=[[Indian Express Limited|ENS]] |date=5 February 2009 |location=[[Pune]] |language=en |access-date=9 October 2022 |url-access=subscription |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241202003821/https://indianexpress.com/article/cities/pune/fugitive-run-ends-for-economic-fraud-and-dreaded-gangster/ |archive-date=2 December 2024}}</ref>

Agashe was taken into [[judicial custody]] in February 2009.<ref name="DNA India 1">{{cite news |title=Mandar Agashe in police custody |work=[[Daily News & Analysis]] |url=https://cataleg.bnc.cat/iii/cas/login?service=https%3A%2F%2Fexplora.bnc.cat%3A443%2Fiii%2Fencore%2Fj_acegi_cas_security_check&lang=eng&suite=def |date=2 May 2009 |via=[[National Library of Catalonia]] |url-access=subscription |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210728205302/https://cataleg.bnc.cat/iii/cas/login?service=https%3A%2F%2Fexplora.bnc.cat%3A443%2Fiii%2Fencore%2Fj_acegi_cas_security_check&lang=eng&suite=def |archive-date=28 July 2021}}</ref> After his father's death, Agashe was approached by former depositors of the bank for repayment of the defaulted loans.<ref>{{cite news |title=Pay back time |url=https://punemirror.com/pune/cover-story/pay-back-time/cid5260744.htm |work=[[Pune Mirror]] |date=5 February 2009 |access-date=9 October 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221011100141/https://punemirror.com/pune/cover-story/pay-back-time/cid5260744.htm |archive-date=11 October 2022}}</ref> In early March 2009, he was remanded to [[Detention (confinement)|magisterial custody]] after his initial [[Bail|plea for bail]] was rejected. He was charged with having sanctioned [[Forgery|forged]] loan proposals amounting to ₹1.13 billion.<ref>{{cite news |title=Mandar Agashe's bail plea rejected |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/pune/Mandar-Agashes-bail-plea-rejected/articleshow/4236853.cms |url-access=subscription |work=[[The Times of India]] |agency=[[Times News Network|TNN]] |date=7 March 2009 |location=[[Pune]] |access-date=9 October 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101222204041/http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/pune/Mandar-Agashes-bail-plea-rejected/articleshow/4236853.cms |archive-date=22 December 2010}}</ref> Agashe was subsequently released on bail on 11 March,<ref>{{cite news |title=Mandar will stay with cops |url=https://punemirror.com/pune/cover-story/mandar-will-stay-with-cops/cid5259604.htm |access-date=19 January 2022 |work=[[Pune Mirror]] |date=7 March 2009 |language=en-IN |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220119211120/https://punemirror.com/pune/cover-story/mandar-will-stay-with-cops/cid5259604.htm |archive-date=19 January 2022}}</ref> but was kept under [[house arrest]] until the bank [[Mergers and acquisitions|merger]] was resolved.<ref name="DNA India 1" /> The bank was eventually [[Dissolution (law)|dissolved]] and merged with the [[Indian Overseas Bank]] in May 2009.<ref>{{cite news |title=IOB posts 17 per cent rise in business |url=https://www.thehindu.com/business/companies/IOB-posts-17-per-cent-rise-in-business/article16889288.ece |work=[[The Hindu]] |access-date=25 August 2022 |date=30 October 2009 |language=en-IN |location=[[Chennai]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210125112652/https://www.thehindu.com/business/companies/IOB-posts-17-per-cent-rise-in-business/article16889288.ece |archive-date=25 January 2021}}</ref>

=== Later business career: 2009–present ===

|url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/finance/we-help-banks-stay-on-the-grid-sarvatra-technologies-mandar-agashe-120050700085_1.html |url-access=subscription |access-date=9 October 2022 |archive-date=12 October 2022}}</ref> the company's [[Electronic funds transfer|financial switch]] helping 450 [[Cooperative banking|co-operative banks]] and 50 urban co-operative banks, by 2018 and by 2020 respectively, connect to India's [[National Electronic Funds Transfer]] service.<ref>{{cite news |title=Sarvatra Technologies brings 450th co-operative bank on National Financial Switch == Musical career ==
[[File:Mandar-agashe-asha-bhosle-april-2016.jpg|Agashe with [[Asha Bhosle]] in April 2016.|thumb|right]]

During his final year in college, Agashe was introduced to [[Hridaynath Mangeshkar]], who invited him to compose music for the [[Shirish Atre-Pai]]-authored [[Marathi poetry|Marathi poem]] ''Khulya Khulya Re Pavasa'' ({{literal translation|Open, Open, Rain}}), sung by [[Asha Bhosle]] for the [[Marathi cinema|Marathi movie]] ''Hey Geet Jeevanache'' (1995). Previously in 1994, Agashe had recorded an English [[rock music]] album in [[Indianapolis]], citing [[The Beatles]] as a major influence.<ref name="Indian Express 1">{{cite news |last1=Mehta |first1=Vibha |title=First Person |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/news-archive/first-person-2/ |access-date=9 October 2022 |work=[[The Indian Express]] |date=20 November 1998 |language=en |url-access=subscription |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221009183900/https://indianexpress.com/article/news-archive/first-person-2/ |archive-date=9 October 2022}}</ref> 

In 1997, Agashe released his first [[Marathi language]] album titled ''Achanak'' ({{literal translation|Suddenly}}).<ref name="Times of India 1">{{Cite news |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/nagpur/asha-renders-six-suresh-bhat-ghazals-to-western-tunes/articleshow/51917554.cms |access-date=9 October 2022 |last1=Mathur |first1=Barkha |title=Asha renders six Suresh Bhat ghazals to western tunes |work=[[The Times of India]] |url-access=subscription |date=21 April 2016 |location=[[Nagpur]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180915125200/https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/nagpur/Asha-renders-six-Suresh-Bhat-ghazals-to-western-tunes/articleshow/51917554.cms |archive-date=15 September 2018}}</ref> In 1998, he released his first [[Hindi|Hindi language]] album titled ''Nazar Nazar'' ({{literal translation|Look, Look}}).<ref name="Indian Express 1" /><ref>{{cite news |last1=Kharade |first1=Pallavi |title=Singing a solo tune |date=30 April 2004 |url=http://epaper.timesofindia.com/Default/Scripting/ArticleWin.asp?From=Search&Key=TOIPU/2004/04/30/24/Ar02401.xml&CollName=TOI_PUNE_ARCHIVE&DOCID=86812&Keyword=%28%28%3Cmany%3E%3Cstem%3EMandar%3Cphrase%3E%3Cmany%3E%3Cstem%3EAgashe%29%29&skin=pastissues2&AppName=2&ViewMode=GIF |access-date=5 January 2022 |work=[[Pune Times]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171225145012/http://epaper.timesofindia.com/Default/Scripting/ArticleWin.asp?From=Search&Key=TOIPU/2004/04/30/24/Ar02401.xml&CollName=TOI_PUNE_ARCHIVE&DOCID=86812&Keyword=%28%28%3Cmany%3E%3Cstem%3EMandar%3Cphrase%3E%3Cmany%3E%3Cstem%3EAgashe%29%29&skin=pastissues2&AppName=2&ViewMode=GIF |archive-date=25 Dec 2017 |url-access=subscription}}</ref> The album was produced by Ashutosh Phatak and [[Dhruv Ghanekar]] and released in India by [[Sony BMG]].<ref>{{Cite AV media |title=Nazar Nazar by Mandar Agashe |publisher=[[Sony BMG]] |year=1998 |place=[[Mumbai]] |type=[[Cassette tape|Cassette]]}}</ref>

In 2003, Agashe released a [[New-age music|new age]]-[[techno]] track titled ''I Need Someone'' in [[Germany]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/pune-times/Mandar-to-release-single-in-Germany/articleshow/130147.cms |title=Mandar to release single in Germany |work=[[The Times of India]] |last=Contractor |first=Huned |agency=[[Times News Network|TNN]] |url-access=subscription |access-date=9 October 2022 |date=14 August 2003 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180901084804/https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/pune-times/Mandar-to-release-single-in-Germany/articleshow/130147.cms |archive-date=1 September 2018}}</ref> In 2005, he further released a [[Double-sided disk|double-sided album]] titled ''Two of Us'' featuring an album of Hindi pop music titled ''Jaan Le'' ({{literal translation|Know It}}) and an album of English rock music titled ''F. C. Road''.<ref>{{cite book |title=Two of Us |location=[[Pune]] |date=2005 |oclc=1135234390 |lccn=2020615057 }}</ref><ref name="Your Tech Story 1">{{cite news |title=Mandar Agashe : The Man Who Brought a Revolution in the Indian Digital Payment System |url=https://www.yourtechstory.com/2019/08/19/mandar-agashe-man-brought-revolution-indian-digital-payment-system/ |work=Your Tech Story |date=19 August 2019 |access-date=9 October 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210729211024/https://www.yourtechstory.com/2019/08/19/mandar-agashe-man-brought-revolution-indian-digital-payment-system/ |archive-date=29 July 2021}}</ref>

In April 2016, Agashe [[Music director|music directed]] a [[pop music|western pop]] album of [[Suresh Bhat]]'s [[ghazal]]s in Marathi with Asha Bhosle called ''82''. The album was titled after Bhosle's age at the time of recording. Recorded within one week, the album consisted of ghazals given to Agashe by Bhat. In a televised launch for the album, hosted by [[Sudhir Gadgil]], Agashe and Bhosle also announced a competition for [[Fan labor|fan-made]] music videos to the songs on the album.<ref name="Times of India 1" /><ref>{{Cite news |url=https://starmarathi.in/asha-bhosale-sings-suresh-bhat-gajhals-for-her-next-album-82/ |access-date=9 October 2022 |title=Asha Bhosale sings Suresh Bhat gajhals for her next album "82" |work=Star Marathi |date=12 April 2016 |language=mr, en |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221012222141/https://starmarathi.in/asha-bhosale-sings-suresh-bhat-gajhals-for-her-next-album-82/ |archive-date=12 October 2022}}</ref>

In June 2021, Agashe music directed a Marathi [[Retro (music)|retro music]] album of Suresh Bhat's poems and ghazals with [[Rahul Deshpande]] titled ''Theek Aahe, Chaan Aahe, Masta Aahe'' ({{literal translation|It's Okay, It's Good, It's Great}}). Recorded during the [[COVID-19 lockdown in India]], the album was produced by Vivek Paranjape and featured [[Aarya Ambekar]], [[Dhanashree Deshpande-Ganatra]], and Pranjali Barve as guest vocalists.<ref>Multiple sources: {{Bulleted list|{{Cite AV media |title=लॉकडाऊनमध्ये साकारला म्युझिक अल्बम |trans-title=Music album made during lockdown |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AWnHNbOJnlg |date=9 June 2021 |type=[[Television special]] |language=mr |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210729211022/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AWnHNbOJnlg |archive-date=29 July 2021 |publisher=[[Sakal]] |access-date=27 April 2025 |via=[[YouTube]]}}|{{cite news |last1=Parchure |first1=Ajay |title='ठीक आहे छान आहे मस्त आहे' म्युझिक अल्बमचे ऑनलाइन कार्यक्रमात प्रकाशन |trans-title=Release of 'Theek Aahe, Chaan Aahe, Masta Aahe' Music Album in Online Event |url=https://www.mumbaitak.in/entertainment/thik-aahe-chan-aahe-music-album-released-online |access-date=9 October 2022 |work=Mumbai Tak |date=28 June 2021 |language=mr |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210628104706/https://www.mumbaitak.in/entertainment/thik-aahe-chan-aahe-music-album-released-online |archive-date=28 June 2021}}|{{cite news |title=सुरेश भट यांच्या कवितांचा म्युझिक अल्बम 'ठीक आहे छान आहे मस्त आहे' झाला प्रकाशित! |url=https://www.etvbharat.com/marathi/maharashtra/sitara/tv-and-theater/suresh-bhatts-music-album-of-poems-thik-aahe-chan-aahe-mast-aahe-has-been-released/mh20210702202055924 |access-date=9 October 2022 |work=[[ETV Network|ETV Bharat]] |date=2 July 2021 |language=mr |trans-title=The music album of Suresh Bhat's poems 'Theek Aahe, Chaan Aahe, Masta Aahe' has been released! |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221010235258/https://www.etvbharat.com/marathi/maharashtra/sitara/tv-and-theater/suresh-bhatts-music-album-of-poems-thik-aahe-chan-aahe-mast-aahe-has-been-released/mh20210702202055924 |archive-date=10 October 2022}}}}</ref>

extract:
Mandar Dnyaneshwar Agashe (born 24 May 1969) is an Indian businessman, music director, and former musician. He founded Sarvatra Technologies in 2000, and has served as the company's managing director since its inception.
As a musician, he is remembered for his pop and rock music releases in Hindi and English under Sony BMG in the 1990s and 2000s, and for music directing Marathi ghazal albums for Asha Bhosle in 2016, and Rahul Deshpande in 2021.
